reply_text:
You should have been alerted, and nothing in the machine or in my reports did it. I've added that as a finding in the incident, together with a table of the critical parameters and their values at click 20 (commit `78e53c492`).

**The critical parameters at click 20:**

| Parameter | Design | Click 20 |
|---|---|---|
| Open tasks that exist | all of them | about 637 by yesterday's census |
| Tasks the decision enumerates | the same set | missions and tickets only; excursions absent |
| Targets that reach scoring | every enumerated target | 3 |
| Targets with a score | every one that reaches scoring | 1 |
| Patterns a cascade may draw on | the library slice for the problem, from about 1,415 | 2 |
| Policies compared | many per target | 1 |
| Preference along the horizon (Cτ) | stated for every step | blank for steps 1–3 |
| Terms of G in use | risk, ambiguity, information gain | risk only |

**On the whitelist.** What the records and `PROOF-2b.md` show is five hand-written target files from 17 September, not three. Four of those targets were later finished. Between 2 and 21 targets had candidates on 20–21 September, and there was one target in almost every record from 22 September onward. So the facade you first noticed and the one-policy facade are the same mechanism, which narrowed over time.

**Why there was no alert.** The machine has thirteen tripwires, T1 to T13, and none of them watches any of these numbers. The values were in every run record and in no report. My own reports to you talked about selections and refusals and never gave the size of what was being chosen among.

**What changes:**

- **My reports.** These eight numbers head every report I make about a run, before anything else is said about it.
- **The machine.** A run whose critical parameters are degenerate raises an alert addressed to you and is not reported as a selection. The report belongs to the records owner and the tripwire to the controller owner. I'll send those handoffs once codex-6's audit is back, because the audit should name the full list of parameters that need watching, and these eight are only the ones I've found so far.

The three jobs in flight are unchanged, all parked: codex-6 on the Lean audit, codex-4 on the selection repair, and codex-5 on the debugger.
